minutes.headline: Board left license fees unchanged for COVID-hit businesses; skate park location and size debated with no vote.
minutes.summary: The Select Board approved the Salvation Army boot drive and, jointly with the Parks Commission, appointed a fifth parks member. A long joint session with the skate park group debated moving the park from beside TC Passios to Marshall Park and its size, with no vote. The board then discussed relief on liquor license fees for COVID-hit businesses and took no action, pointing businesses to a regional recovery fund. The town manager gave a mid-year goals update and a report.

what_happened.line: The Select Board took no action on a request to lower liquor license fees for COVID-hit businesses and pointed them to regional recovery funds.
A long joint session on the skate park debated moving it from beside TC Passios to Marshall Park, and its size; no vote was taken.
The board and Parks Commission appointed Anna Lockwood as the fifth Parks Commission member; the vote was stated as seven to zero with one abstention.
The board approved the Salvation Army boot drive request for Dec 12 by roll call.
The board nominated Michael Ray Jeffries as its MART appointee, and a meeting on the old primary school was targeted for January 12.

why_it_matters: License fees stay as they are, so local businesses hurt by COVID get no fee cut from the town. The fees are built into local receipts in the budget, and the town manager's help with recovery funds is the route offered instead.
The skate park's site and size are still open. Moving it to Marshall Park would change which park land and which project costs residents are asked to support.
